cohort: 299 neonates suspected of neonatal sepsis admitted to the sick neonatal wards and neonatal intensive care unit of Burdwan Medical College from March 2017 to February 2018.
finding: Klebsiella spp. (33.8%) and Staphylococcus aureus (25.8%) were the most common bacterial isolates in neonates with sepsis, and resistance to conventional antibiotics like amoxicillin, cephalosporins, and piperacillin-tazobactam was alarmingly high.
birth_weight: Low birth weight neonates represented 37.29% of the sample.
